title: Recovering Markov Generators and Causal Risks from Transitions Observed at Gamma Random Times
banked_reason: The exact three- and four-state Gamma-clock frontiers are sound, but the delivered known-clock population-identification package is capped at subfield and is not salvageable at the field floor within scope.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived and independently audited exact Gamma-clock injectivity thresholds at alpha 6 in three states and alpha 4 in four states, endpoint-safe principal-power recovery for defective generators, an all-dimensional sufficient recovery region, and open positive-rate alias families with separated fixed-time risks. The mathematics and citation audits passed with no unrepaired findings, but the field-tier case collapsed on scope and payoff rather than correctness. A future re-raise must begin from a new root: a sharp n>=5 frontier or a genuine estimation and inference theory.
tldr: With a known Gamma rate and all timestamp-free transition rows available, every finite \(n\geq3\) has the explicit safe region \(0<\alpha\leq2n/(n-2)\): throughout it, including the endpoint and defective generators, \(Q=\lambda[I_n-K^{-1/\alpha}]\), so the recovered generator identifies every fixed-calendar occupancy risk and randomized-arm contrast. Consequently \(0<\alpha\leq2\) is uniformly safe over all finite dimensions. In dimensions three and four the one-sided sector guarantee is sharp: the exact cutoffs are six and four, and above them full-dimensional open sets of positive simple-spectrum generator twins have the same released visit law but different risks. No converse is asserted for \(n\geq5\). Retained timestamps, an unknown clock rate, missing starting-state rows, coarsened informative timing, and local numerical conditioning remain distinct information or stability regimes rather than exceptions to this theorem.
gap: Random-gap CTMC work already identifies the averaged operator and estimates it consistently, but the closest paper does not decide whether complex generator modes can be uniquely inverted. Baake and Sumner's 2024 low-dimensional exponential-embedding classification concerns fibers of \(R\mapsto e^R\), not the restricted shifted-log fibers induced by \(Q\mapsto(I-Q/\lambda)^{-\alpha}\). General embedding and root results do not impose the joint constraints \(Q\mathbf1=0\), nonnegative rates, a fixed Gamma shape, and recovery of calendar-time risks, and no inspected source states the proposed \(6/4\) boundaries.
fill: Prove the complete three-state scalar-transform criterion, the sharp three- and four-state Gamma frontier including defective spectra and endpoints, an explicit principal-power inverse, exact auditable twins, and an open-family nonidentification theorem whose Fréchet derivatives, reality, strict positivity, and risk separation are all certified on one common neighborhood; state the distinct information regimes and a proportionate local sensitivity bound.
